catalog_quote: [Swadesh 1946: 114] The sounds represented by the remaining symbols are fairly typical and may be passed over except to mention that e° represents a very open sound, close to the English vowel in cat. Accent is a purely mechanical function of phrase rhythm: phrases are normally accented on the last syllable. The Atakapa material includes forms from three dialects: the bulk is Western Atakapa (shown as At. or W.) recorded in 1885 by Gatschet with a few later additions by Swanton ... [p. 115] Evidently reflecting the accentual weakness of open, non-final syllables, are a number of cases in which such syllables are found with and without initial h; thus, hipa, ipa husband. In giving words of this type, we show only the writing with h. Likewise in open, non-final syllables, we find a few cases of variant vowel writing: yemoy, yimop cheap; temak, timak knee ... [Gatschet & Swanton 1932: 6] A…

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: every quoted passage is verbatim in the held files at the stated pages (only the Kaufman 2014 locator should read pp. 77-78, not p. 75). The classification PHRASAL/PHRASE rests on Swadesh 1946, a comparative phonology article reinterpreting Gatschet's 1885 notes, with the accent claim a single hedged sentence ('normally') in a paragraph covering both Atakapa and Chitimacha.
